traps.name: Kendra/Lex as RAG distractors
traps.pattern: On Bedrock-context RAG questions, Kendra and Lex appear as plausible-looking answer options.
traps.spot_it: If the scenario is Bedrock-centric and asks for managed RAG → answer is almost always Bedrock Knowledge Bases. Lex is for chatbot front-ends, not FM orchestration. Kendra is enterprise search, not the Bedrock-native RAG path.
traps.source: Greciano beta-passer notes; multiple community reports

traps.name: Comprehend over-emphasis in practice exams
traps.pattern: Third-party practice tests over-feature Comprehend; the real exam tests it lightly.
traps.spot_it: Don't pick Comprehend just because it sounds AI-related. Use it only for: PII detection in pipelines (where Guardrails is overkill), sentiment, entity extraction on non-FM workflows.

traps.name: Fine-tune vs RAG framing
traps.pattern: Stem describes 'company data the model should know about' — both fine-tune and RAG sound plausible.
traps.spot_it: Data CHANGES (weekly/daily, new docs) → RAG. Data is STATIC and you need STYLE/FORMAT/TASK adaptation → fine-tune. New DOMAIN VOCAB without labels → continued pre-training. Never fine-tune for facts that update.

traps.name: Bedrock Agents vs Step Functions
traps.spot_it: FM reasoning decides next step → Bedrock Agents. Deterministic predefined workflow with branching → Step Functions. If the stem says 'LLM picks which tool to call', it's Agents.

traps.name: Provisioned Throughput trap on bursty workloads
traps.pattern: Stem says 'guarantee capacity' and you reach for Provisioned Throughput.
traps.spot_it: PT is a 1mo/6mo commit — overkill (and expensive) for bursty/seasonal workloads. For bursty: on-demand baseline + scale; for steady high volume: PT. PT is REQUIRED for custom (fine-tuned) model hosting.

traps.name: PrivateLink vs VPC interface endpoints
traps.pattern: 'Private connectivity to Bedrock' — multiple wordings appear.
traps.spot_it: Bedrock supports AWS PrivateLink via VPC interface endpoints for bedrock, bedrock-runtime, bedrock-agent, bedrock-agent-runtime. These are the SAME thing — different exam phrasings. NAT Gateway is NOT a private path.

traps.name: Guardrails vs IAM scoping
traps.pattern: Question conflates 'restrict what the model can talk about' with 'restrict who can call the model'.
traps.spot_it: Guardrails = CONTENT policy (what the FM may say/process). IAM = ACCESS policy (who may invoke). Need both for defense in depth. Question that says 'block topics' → Guardrails. 'Block users' → IAM.

traps.name: Multi-region inference profile vs cross-region replication
traps.spot_it: Inference profile = ONE ARN routes traffic across regions for resilience/capacity. Cross-region replication = COPYING data (S3, custom model weights) across regions for DR. Don't confuse them.

traps.name: 'Reduce hallucinations' signature
traps.pattern: Stem asks to reduce hallucinations — many options sound plausible.
traps.spot_it: Top 3 levers in order: (1) RAG with KBs (ground in your data), (2) Guardrails CONTEXTUAL GROUNDING check (auto-block low-grounded responses), (3) lower temperature/top_p. Fine-tuning RARELY helps with hallucinations.

traps.name: Multi-response 'Select TWO/THREE' counting
traps.pattern: Multi-response questions state how many to pick; getting the count wrong = auto-fail of that Q.
traps.spot_it: Read the LAST line of the stem. Count YOUR selected boxes vs the stated number BEFORE submitting. Multi-response is partial-credit-NONE — all-or-nothing.

traps.name: Lowest-latency RAG retrieval
traps.pattern: Multiple vector stores listed as options.
traps.spot_it: Sub-ms in-memory → MemoryDB. Default low-ops → OpenSearch Serverless vector. Reuse existing Postgres → Aurora pgvector. Graph + vector → Neptune Analytics. If 'low ops' AND 'integrated with Bedrock KBs', it's OpenSearch Serverless.

traps.name: Bedrock prompt caching cost trap
traps.spot_it: Cache WRITE costs ~1.25x base; cache READ costs ~0.1x base. Break-even ≈ 2-3 reuses of the cached prefix. Don't cache prefixes that won't be reused soon. 5-min TTL.

traps.name: Batch inference window
traps.spot_it: Batch is ASYNC with up to 24h SLA — never the right answer for real-time/interactive use cases. It IS the right answer for: large offline jobs, nightly summarization, eval datasets, where 50% cost saving matters.

traps.name: Knowledge Base chunking choice
traps.pattern: Options offer fixed, semantic, hierarchical, default chunking.
traps.spot_it: Default = quick start (300 tokens, 20% overlap). Fixed = predictable size. Semantic = group by meaning (better recall for narrative docs). Hierarchical = parent-child for long structured docs (legal, manuals). Pick by document structure, not by 'sounds advanced'.

traps.name: Model evaluation type confusion
traps.pattern: Bedrock Model Evaluation has Automated, Human (in-house team), LLM-as-judge.
traps.spot_it: Quick + reproducible + standard datasets → Automated. Subjective quality, brand voice → Human in-house team. Scale + flexible criteria + cheaper than human → LLM-as-judge. Don't pick 'Human (AWS team)' — that doesn't exist for general evaluation.

tips: 2.5 min/Q hard cap. Flag and move. Come back at the end.
Read the LAST line of the stem first (the actual ask), then re-read the scenario with that ask in mind.
Eliminate the 2 obviously-wrong options FAST. The remaining pair is where the real decision lives.
'Most cost-effective' + 'managed' → almost always a Bedrock-native feature, not a hand-rolled pipeline.
'Lowest latency for retrieval' → OpenSearch Serverless vector or MemoryDB; not Aurora pgvector unless DB already exists.
Multi-response: count YOUR selections vs the stated number before submitting. All-or-nothing scoring.

If two options look identical in spirit but one mentions a CONCRETE AWS service (Bedrock KBs, OpenSearch Serverless, Lambda) and the other is generic ('a custom pipeline'), the concrete one usually wins.
When in doubt between two managed services, pick the one in the SAME service family as the rest of the scenario (e.g., scenario is Bedrock-heavy → pick the Bedrock-native option).
'No code changes' or 'minimize developer effort' → Guardrails, Knowledge Bases, Agents — managed features, not custom Lambda.
Questions with 'AT REST' / 'IN TRANSIT' framing → KMS (CMK), TLS, PrivateLink. Identify which one the question is actually asking about.
Questions about 'auditing FM usage' → CloudTrail (control plane) + Model invocation logging (data plane). Both, often.
Trust your first read. Changing answers at the end usually decreases accuracy.
exam_room: Test-center > online proctor for stamina (passer consensus). Quick bathroom breaks allowed at test centers.
180 min is shorter than you think for 75 questions. Don't camp on one question.
Use 'Mark for Review' aggressively on the first pass. Speed > perfection on pass 1.
Pass 2: revisit marked questions with the time you saved. New context from later Qs sometimes unlocks earlier ones.
If the question is incoherent or seems wrong, it's probably an unscored experimental Q. Pick the best plausible answer and MOVE ON.
Drink water before, not during. Caffeine that lasts 4h not 1h.
Read each option fully before picking — close-distractor traps live in the last clause of an option.
